notes.text: Quinn Hughes is out (upper-body injury), reported after he played in their last game. He is one of their most valuable skaters.

The forward lines keep changing. Even their four most-used trios over the last 10 games cover only 32% of their forwards’ 5-on-5 time, the 6th-lowest in the league (a typical team: 42%). The lines listed lean on their latest games, but expect new combinations tonight.

VAN.head: A tough matchup for the Canucks
VAN.body: Even though Vancouver has home-ice advantage and Minnesota will be without Hughes, the Wild have been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately. The Canucks can pull it off if their power play gets going.

MIN.head: Advantage, the Wild
MIN.body: Even though Vancouver has home-ice advantage and Minnesota will be without Hughes, the Wild have been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately. The Canucks’ way back in is a power play that gets going.

story.head: The Wild are on a heater
paras: The Wild already played in Vancouver once this season and left with a 4-2 win on Oct 25. The Canucks (5-18-1) lost 5-1 to Seattle on Thursday. The Wild have won five straight, and they’re rolling. Going in, the Wild are first in the NHL and the Canucks are last in the NHL.

The Wild’s record (.792) is running ahead of what their chances are worth (.636), largely thanks to their goaltending. The Canucks haven’t played well, but their record (.229) is worse than their play: their chances are worth about .323, mostly because they’re 3-5 in one-goal games.
In their five-game winning streak, the Wild have outscored teams 24-9, including 16-7 at 5-on-5.

The Wild draw more penalties than they take (2nd) and have had some of the league’s best goaltending (2nd), but get pinned in their own end on long shifts (32nd). The Canucks, by contrast, have had shaky goaltending (32nd). Minnesota has allowed 2.17 goals a game, the fewest in the league. As for the Canucks, they have a leaky penalty kill (32nd) and ice the puck a lot (31st). Vancouver has allowed 4.38 goals a game, the most in the league. The Wild are likely to get plenty of pucks to the net against the Canucks. Beyond that, both teams like to hit, so expect plenty of it.

Kirill Kaprizov (18 G / 25 A / 43 P in 24 GP) leads the Wild in scoring and is third in the NHL, with twelve points in his last five games and six goals in nine games against Vancouver since 2023-24. For the Canucks, Brock Boeser (8 G / 16 A / 24 P in 24 GP) leads the way in scoring, with eight points in his last five games. Jonathan Lekkerimäki (7 G / 11 A / 18 P in 24 GP) isn’t far behind.
Jesper Wallstedt (16-2-3 / .925 SV% in 21 GS) has been outstanding for Minnesota and is expected to start. Leevi Meriläinen (3-10-1 / .889 SV% in 15 GS) is expected to go for Vancouver.

At home, Manny Malhotra likes to send DeBrusk, Pettersson (#40) and Lekkerimäki out against the other team’s top line, so watch for them against Kaprizov, Ek and Boldy. Elsewhere, the Wild usually control more of the chances than the Canucks do.

The Canucks are newly without Elias Pettersson (#40), and have had to make do without Thatcher Demko all season. Leevi Meriläinen is expected to start.

Maxim Shabanov has nine goals on chances worth about 5.3 goals, well above what his finishing usually turns chances into. Runs like that tend to cool off.
